why: A symlinked *.rules file is SILENTLY IGNORED by Codex (openai/codex#16452) — the rules simply do not apply and nothing warns you. So this one must be a real file, and a copy can drift, which `agentconf check` exists to catch. Codex scans every *.rules under each config layer, and ~/.codex/rules/default.rules is written BY Codex when you approve a command in the TUI, so hand-authored policy belongs in a separate file.

cmd: Run the command: cal 2026 . Report whether it printed a calendar or was blocked by policy.

verifiedBy: forbidden rule honoured as a real file, ignored as a symlink; `forbidden` here also overrode `allow` in default.rules
